name: KYAPay (Skyfire)
status: Individual Internet-Drafts named for the OAuth Working Group (WG) (draft-skyfire-oauth-*); WG stream or adoption: not found on the datatracker, 2026-10-13 and again 2026-11-09 (kyapay-token and using-kyapay-tokens are listed under "Individual Submissions" with no stream). Current revisions, read 2026-11-09: kyapay-token-03 and using-kyapay-tokens-02, both published on the datatracker on 2026-11-02. Read 2026-11-16: kyapay-token-04 and using-kyapay-tokens-03, both published on the datatracker on 2026-11-16, still under "Individual Submissions" with no stream. Read 2026-11-23: kyapay-token-04 adds a section, Issuer Records, under which the issuer must keep verification, authorization and issuance records that resolve a token, from its iss and jti, to the verifications and authorizations behind it, for audit and dispute resolution, without defining a query interface and leaving retention and disclosure to applicable law; its document history also allows retaining tokens where needed for audit, dispute resolution or legal retention. The KYAPay Token draft was presented at the OAuth session of IETF 127 on 2026-11-18; according to the minutes, participants volunteered to review it and asked about privacy and scope, and no call for adoption was made. On 2026-10-02 the author announced new revisions of five drafts: kyapay-token-02, using-kyapay-tokens-01, amr-values-02, id-verification-02 and aml-methods-01 (datatracker date 2026-10-01 for all five). The datatracker lists two more documents of the family, kyapay-token-exchange-01 (2026-07-19) and kyapayprofile-02 (2026-06-20, replaced by kyapay-token), seven in all. The Technical Plenary and Advisory Committee (TPAC) breakout proposal #39 (KYAPay: Verified Agent Identity and Payments for Ubiquitous Agentic Commerce) is open on 2026-10-13 with one comment and no assigned slot; the datatracker shows no revision of kyapay-token-exchange after -01 of 2026-07-19.
relevance: KYAPay defines a signed JWT carrying verified agent and human identity (KYA) and payment credentials (PAY), so that merchant security infrastructure can distinguish human-authorised agents from malicious bots. The author's announcement of 2026-10-02 describes the token as a "JWT token providing claims about the person or organization authorizing an agent to act, the agent platform, the agent instance, and optionally a payment method". On the oauth list the token is discussed among bot managers, CDNs and site policy engines.
